topic: CA: Writing a Profile — Peer Edit Workshop
objective: By the end of the lesson, learners will have given and received peer feedback on their profile drafts using a 3-point checklist (capitalisation, compound sentences, the hook) and produced a revised version incorporating that feedback.
materials:
- Students' first drafts from the previous lesson
- Projector (for comparison paragraphs and model edit)
- Timer visible to the class
- Optional: coloured pens / pencils if available

stages.stage: Lead-in — Three things we have been working on
stages.stage_aim: To reactivate prior knowledge of capitalisation, compound sentences, and the hook, and to show students how these three areas make the difference between a weak first draft and a strong final article.
stages.procedure: - Project two versions of the opening of an article about learning to play football (a completely different topic from the students' own profile). Version A has capitalisation errors, all simple sentences, and a weak hook. Version B is corrected in all three areas. Pairs discuss: 'Which version is better? Why?' Elicit the three editing criteria: (1) capitalisation, (2) compound sentences, (3) the hook. Frame the lesson: 'Today you will swap drafts with a partner and check each other's work for exactly these three things.'

stages.stage: Model Edit — Watch me check a draft
stages.stage_aim: To demonstrate exactly how to check for capitalisation, compound sentences, and the hook using a think-aloud, so students know what to look for and how to mark it.
stages.procedure: - Project a sample paragraph about learning to bake a cake (another parallel topic — not football, not a profile). The paragraph has capitalisation errors, no compound sentences, and a weak hook. Teacher thinks aloud through all three checks, showing the marking system: C circle (capital needed), crossed-out capital (no capital needed), boxed coordinator, +coord (comma splice), and hook? marker. Clarify: 'You are not fixing your partner's draft. You are leaving marks and notes. They decide what to change.'

stages.stage_aim: To give each student a reader's perspective on their draft through two focused passes — first for overall understanding, then for the three editing criteria.
stages.procedure:
- Students swap drafts with a partner.
**Pass 1 — Read for understanding (7 minutes):** Read silently. Mark ✓ for clear parts, ? for confusing parts. Do not correct anything yet.
**Pass 2 — Three-check edit (13 minutes):** Apply the three checks: (1) Capitalisation — circle missing capitals (C), cross out unnecessary capitals, check 'I' is always capital, check apostrophes in contractions. (2) Compound sentences — box every coordinator (and, but, so, or), mark comma splices with +coord, suggest combining short sentences. (3) The hook — read the first sentence. ★ = strong hook, hook? = needs work.
- After 20 minutes, students return the draft to its owner.

stages.stage: Final Polish — Your turn to revise
stages.stage_aim: To give students time to read their partner's feedback and produce a clean final version of their profile, deciding for themselves which changes to make.
stages.procedure: - Students look at their own draft with their partner's marks. Three things to check: (1) Capitalisation — fix every circled letter and crossed-out capital. (2) Compound sentences — fix comma splices, aim for at least 1 compound sentence. (3) The hook — revise the first sentence if marked hook?; try a question or a bold statement. Teacher circulates and prompts with questions. Students write or type the final version. Collect both drafts for teacher assessment.
